title: A fasta header with a tab after the name puts the tab inside the target name
body:
`Sequence::from_fasta` in `libnail/src/structs/sequence.rs` ends a record's name at the first space only. A header such as `>abc<TAB>some desc` gives the name `abc<TAB>some` and the details `desc`. libsail's `seq::fasta::name_of`, which names the record for nail's index and repeated-name check, ends the name at any ASCII whitespace and gives `abc`. Easel's `header_fasta` in `esl_sqio_ascii.c` does the same with `isspace`.

The tabular output takes the target name from `Sequence::name`, through `with_target_name(&target.name)` in `align_stage.rs`. So the wrong name reaches the results without any error. With the first space of every header in `fixtures/target.fa` turned into a tab, nail exits 0. 405 of its 408 rows carry the name, a tab, and the first word of the description as the target name, for example `O08858|reviewed|Somatostatin<TAB>receptor`. That adds a tab inside a field of a tab-separated row.

## Proposal

End the name at any ASCII whitespace, as libsail and Easel do, and start the details after the run of whitespace that follows it.

## Open

- Whether `from_fasta` should take the name from libsail's `name_of` instead of finding it itself, so the two can't disagree again.
